title: Language, Culture, and Ideology: Personalizing Offensiveness Detection in Political Tweets with Reasoning LLMs

bias_targets.methodology: Prompting large language models with distinct political personas (far-right, moderate conservative, centrist, progressive left) to classify political tweets as offensive or non-offensive, and using correlation matrices and an Inter-Group Differentiation (IGD) metric to measure how well the models separate and simulate these ideological viewpoints.

Varying the stated nationality of the simulated persona (American, Polish, Russian) alongside the prompt language to assess cross-cultural consistency and differences in offensiveness judgments using a Cross-Language Consistency (CLC) metric.

Evaluating the language used in the models' internal reasoning traces when prompted in non-English languages (Polish, Russian), measuring the frequency with which the models default to generating reasoning in English.
